hero.subtitle: If you were hurt while working in Kerman, from a Madera Avenue warehouse to a Whitesbridge Road farm operation, understanding whether workers' comp or a third-party claim applies can be confusing. We can help you sort through it at no cost.

about.title: Kerman Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Kerman's economy runs on agriculture, distribution, and small manufacturing, and workplace injuries here often happen around equipment, vehicles, or property owned by someone other than your direct employer. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the only remedy against your employer no matter who caused the accident, but that doesn't close every door. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a road like Rt 180 or California Avenue contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. Fresno County workers deserve to understand both paths before signing anything or letting a claim quietly lapse. Our team reviews the details and explains what options actually exist for your situation, free of charge.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Automatically Ruled Out
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, many injured workers assume that's the end of the story. We can evaluate whether a negligent third party, like a contractor or equipment maker, opens up an additional path to recovery.

items.title: The 30-Day Reporting Window Matters
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report a workplace injury to their employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. Getting a case review early helps make sure paperwork deadlines aren't the reason a valid claim gets denied.

items.title: Retaliation for Reporting Is Illegal
items.desc: Some workers hesitate to report an injury out of fear it could affect their job. California law prohibits employer retaliation for reporting a workplace injury, and we can advise on protecting your position while you pursue the benefits you're entitled to.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Whitesbridge Road but my employer says it's not their problem. What now?
items.answer: If another company's equipment, subcontractor, or negligence contributed to your injury, that may support a third-party claim separate from your workers' comp benefits. We can look at who was actually responsible before you accept your employer's version of events. A free case review is available either way.

items.question: Does workers' comp cover everything, or can I also sue someone?
items.answer: Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer in California regardless of fault, meaning you typically can't sue your employer directly. However, if a third party like a property owner, contractor, or equipment manufacturer caused or contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that party may be available. We can determine whether your situation qualifies.

items.question: How long do I have to act on a workplace injury in Kerman?
items.answer: You generally need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' comp rights. If a third-party claim is involved, California's statute of limitations for that type of injury claim is typically two years from the date of the incident. Waiting too long can limit your options, so it's worth getting a free case review sooner rather than later.
